correctness.rationale: For each n≥2 and J,κ>0, the no-jump L=-iH-κQ/2 on a uniform n-site path is Hurwitz: a purported imaginary-axis eigenvector would have terminal amplitude zero, and the path recurrence then forces all entries zero. Thus integrated survival Gramian M solves L†M+ML=-I uniquely. The explicit parity-defined F,G,C obey [S,F]=0, i[S,C]−{Q,F}/2=−I, i[S,G]=2{Q,C}, {Q,G}=0. Substitution proves M=F/κ+κG/(4J²)+C/J for ALL n. F is positive definite and G semidefinite with kernel span{|n>}, via parity-block Brownian bridge kernels. Consequently Tρ=a/κ+κb/(4J²)+c/J for arbitrary density ρ, unique finite κ*=2J sqrt(a/b) if b>0; for ρ=|n><n|, T=n/κ has no finite minimum. Opposite-parity coherences affect only rate-independent c. Independently checked all four identities and full Lyapunov matrix equation with exact rational sympy arithmetic for dimensions 2..9, rather than trusting saved logs.
